d: a large, curved knife employed in cutting ripe grain or grapes
a bar or frame of wood by which two draft animals are joined at the head or neck in order to work together effectively in pulling a plow, harrow, or wagon
a pointed stick used in driving draft animals
a fork-like shovel for throwing threshed grain into the air so that the wind may separate the chaff from the grain

items used to control the actions of a horse, consisting of a bit (a short metal bar placed in the mouth of a horse) and bridle (ropes or leather straps attached to the bit and fitted over the horse’s head)
a flat triangular blade (the “plowshare”) made of hard wood or metal, connected to a handle; used to cut the soil in preparation for the sowing of seed or the planting of seedlings
